name: Memphis Grizzlies
headline: The Grizzlies are 4-0 behind a Ty Jerome scoring explosion and a pair of nail-biter wins.
good: Memphis is 4-0 and outscoring teams by 9.8 points a game (116.8 to 107.0), with a 114.6 offensive rating against a 105.0 defensive rating.
Ty Jerome is averaging 29.8 points and 6.2 assists on 63.6% true shooting, including a career-high 45 in the 123-103 opener over Utah and 31 on 14-of-14 free throws against Sacramento.

The supporting cast is efficient: Jaylen Wells is at 14.8 points on 60% shooting, Cedric Coward is at 12.7 points and 9.7 rebounds with 72.7% from three, and Zach Edey is blocking 2.0 shots in 21.3 minutes.
The team shoots 39.3% from three and 82.8% from the line, and rebounds 49.5 to 43.0 per game.
bad: Rookie Cameron Boozer is filling the stat sheet (15.2 points, 10.5 rebounds, 4.8 assists) but shooting just 29.5% from the field and 26.9% from three, a 44.0% true shooting mark.

Two of the four wins were close: 111-108 at Golden State after trailing by 12 with under four minutes left, and 110-105 over Utah. The team's own rating model still has Memphis at -1.4, so the margin may be flattering.
Jerome carries a 33% usage rate and the bench is thin on impact: Cam Spencer is a team-worst -24 in total plus/minus.
fans: The comeback in San Francisco got the most attention. Memphis ran off a 17-0 stretch and Boozer hit the go-ahead jumper with 20 seconds left, while Stephen Curry said the Warriors would think about that fourth quarter for a while and Steve Kerr pointed to moving-screen calls among 19 turnovers. Coverage frames Jerome's 45-point opener as a franchise record, topping Ja Morant's 44. I could not find a team subreddit thread in my searches, so I can't say how fans feel beyond the game coverage.
outlook: The 4-0 start is real, but the shooting luck and close finishes suggest some regression, especially if Jerome's usage stays this high. Next up is Thursday at Portland (tip is 2:00 UTC on Oct 30), where the Blazers are 2-0 and the model gives Memphis only a 30.7% chance to win.
